subject: Post-call: hyperscaler parity deep-dive & AB probe asks
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-20T10:15:00Z
Subject: Post-call: hyperscaler parity deep-dive & AB probe asks

Quick recap from the Stratus call this morning (Ellen + their infra lead): they want a short, tightly scoped A/B run to compare Redwood against HyperscalerX's managed inference for their customer-facing chat use case. High-level asks from Stratus:

- p95/p99 latency for 1-2 concurrent sessions at target payloads (avg prompt length ~320 tokens, completions ~180 tokens)
- sustained tokens/sec and tokens/sec per GPU at 1k, 5k, and 10k concurrent tokens windows
- cost-per-1M-tokens estimate for our recommended config vs HyperscalerX
- clear reproduction steps + credentials so they can validate in their environment

My suggested AB matrix (minimal):
1) Redwood default runtime (continuous batching + KV cache warm)
2) Redwood quantized variant (to show cost/latency tradeoff)
3) HyperscalerX managed endpoint (their baseline)

KPIs to measure: p95, p99, median, tokens/sec, error rate (429/5xx), and cold-start tail. Target thresholds they mentioned: p95 < 300ms, p99 < 800ms for typical short-turn tasks; we'll validate with the actual workload generators they shared.

Asks for you both:
- Jordan: can you draft a concrete test harness (load generator config + seed prompt set) and estimate how many GPUs we'll need for a 30-minute sustained run at the 10k token window?
- Marissa: can you pull together the short one-pager we can send Stratus that highlights 3 differentiators we want them to notice during the run (latency tail, batching efficiency, graceful fallback)?

I attached my call notes and the rough timeline Ellen asked for. They want the first run by next Tuesday (12/24) midday PST if possible.

Thanks,
Dylan

Attachments:
- stratus_call_notes.pdf (call notes, prospect requirements)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-20T12:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: hyperscaler parity deep-dive & AB probe asks

Thanks — copying in the minimal test matrix below and a rough resource estimate.

On Mon, Dec 20, 2026 at 10:15 AM Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick recap from the Stratus call this morning...

Proposed test harness (short):
- Load generator: k6 with a custom token-aware driver (seed set = 5k prompts from their corpus)
- Traffic profile: 60% short-turn (<200 tokens), 30% medium (200-500), 10% long (>500)
- Concurrency targets: emulate sliding-window tokens to hit the 1k / 5k / 10k active tokens working set
- Measurement: prometheus + jaeger traces; sample raw outputs for quality spot-checks

Resource estimate (rough):
- For Redwood default: 2 x A100 equivalent GPUs for 30-minute sustained at 10k active tokens (we can scale down to 1 for lower windows); expect tokens/sec ~ 18k-25k total across GPUs depending on prompt mix
- For quantized variant: similar throughput but CPU offload may reduce GPU utilization and lower cost by ~25% (needs validation)

I'll post a public Drive link with the k6 config and target scripts (uploads in ~90m). If we need to hit 12/24, we should schedule a run in our staging cluster tonight so we have a clean artifact to share. Also recommend we provision a HyperscalerX baseline run (I can spin a small job) — need a contact/credentials from Stratus for that.

Jordan
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-21T09:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: hyperscaler parity deep-dive & AB probe asks

Great notes. A couple of things to make the prospect motion smoother:

- Differentiators to highlight during the run (short bullets we can include in the one-pager):
  • Prefix/KV cache warmups reduce p95 by up to 45% for repeat sessions
  • Continuous batching maintains higher tokens/sec under mixed-turn traffic vs fixed-batch approaches
  • Smart routing & fallback: can route lower-tier traffic to a quantized variant automatically to save cost without impacting tail latency for critical sessions

- Quick commercial framing: show them cost delta at 1M tokens and at 10M tokens (we should prepare two numbers: default config and optimized quantized config).

I started the AB matrix spreadsheet and uploaded it (redwood_ab_matrix.csv). I'll draft the 1-pager and share a 1-page PDF for approval before we send to Ellen.

Also — we should pre-stage credentials for HyperscalerX runs. Ellen, if you can connect us to whoever runs their infra benchmark or provide a short-lived token, that'll speed things up.

-Marissa

On Mon, Dec 20, 2026 at 12:03 PM Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com> wrote:
> Proposed test harness...
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@stratus.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Matt Rivera <matt.rivera@stratus.com>
Date: 2026-12-21T15:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: hyperscaler parity deep-dive & AB probe asks

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear plan — this is exactly what we were hoping for. A few confirmations from our side:

- The p95/p99 targets you listed look reasonable as test gates. We'll also be tracking per-customer-session tails (we see big variance across some of our power users).
- We can provide a tokenized subset of our production prompts (anonymized) — I'll have my infra lead send a secure S3 link by EOD.
- For HyperscalerX credentials: cc'd Matt (procurement) — he will coordinate access and handle any procurement redlines.
- Timeline: we prefer the first run on 12/24 in the midday PST window; if that slips, we'll take a run on 12/27.

Attached is our SOC2 access request and a short spreadsheet with the prompt mix (sensitive columns stripped). Please send back the HyperscalerX repro steps and any service accounts we need to provision.

Looking forward to the runs — once we have numbers we'll set a short follow-up to go over the plots (p95/p99 vs tokens/sec) and cost deltas.

Best,
Ellen
